audit_findings.title: The anchor may embed a reversible inventory prebuy as a permanent earnings collapse
audit_findings.magnitude: $118.7 million filed working-capital cash-flow decrease, equal to 106.7% of the $111.2 million anchor; reversible portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A timing-driven inventory increase reduces current owner earnings and, because the valuation compounds the latest-year anchor, depresses every forecast year and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The decrease in cash flows from operating assets and liabilities was primarily attributable to: • $118.7 million decrease in cash flows from working capital due to the pull-forward of inventory purchases at pre-tariff rates relative to the prior year period; and • $20.6 million decrease in cash flows from accounts receivable due to timing of payments received; partially offset by • $37.0 million increase in cash flows from prepaid expenses and other current assets, largely driven by timing of construction reimbursement payments received.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that pre-tariff inventory purchases reduced annual working-capital cash flow by $118.7 million, but it does not establish how much is reversible or how much the $111.2 million calculation retained. The amount is reasonably capable of changing the conclusion: a full-addback sensitivity, without treating it as a recommended adjustment, would raise base value from $28.60 to approximately $53.70 per share. Permanent tariff costs and recurring inventory needed for store growth cannot be added back.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $111.2 million owner earnings line by line, trace the inventory and payable movements, and rerun all scenarios using separately supported reversible, recurring-growth, and permanent-tariff components.

audit_findings.title: Signed but uncommenced leases may not be represented in historical owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $317.0 million filed undiscounted future minimum lease payments; valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Future rent, pre-opening expense, ramp losses, and cannibalization reduce forecast owner earnings associated with new-store growth.
audit_findings.evidence: As of January 31, 2026, the future minimum lease payments on these leases approximated $ 317.0 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The $317.0 million is outside the recognized lease-liability payment schedule but is included in the filed $2.368 billion total operating-lease commitments. Historical owner earnings appropriately exclude rent before possession, but the valuation's aggregate growth assumptions do not show whether the corresponding future costs and new-store sales were modeled together. The record therefore cannot establish the net value effect or its materiality.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a store-cohort forecast reconciling signed locations to sales, rent, pre-opening costs, ramp losses, capital requirements, and cannibalization; rerun growth scenarios without separately deducting lease payments already included in forecast owner earnings.

audit_findings.title: Sale-leaseback gains may have been treated as recurring operating earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $7.1 million and $15.4 million filed gains for 2024 and 2025, totaling $22.5 million; the 2025 gain is 13.8% of the $111.2 million anchor before tax
audit_findings.mechanism: If the gains remain in owner earnings, a nonrecurring property monetization is compounded through forecast earnings and terminal value while related proceeds may also remain in bridge cash.
audit_findings.evidence: We determined that the transactions met the accounting criteria for sale-leaseback treatment and we recognized net gains of approximately $ 7.1 million and $ 15.4 million in SG&A expenses on the Consolidated Statements of Income for 2024 and 2025, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The gains are demonstrated, but their retention in the owner-earnings series is unresolved because no line-by-line calculation was supplied. Using the filed 22.5% effective tax rate, the 2025 gain contributed approximately $11.9 million after tax; if retained, removing it would reduce base value by approximately $2.52 per share. That is large enough to require a rerun even though it would reinforce, rather than reverse, the current conclusion that market price exceeds modeled value.
audit_findings.action: Trace both gains through net income and owner-earnings adjustments, remove any retained after-tax gain, verify treatment of sale proceeds in bridge cash, retain subsequent rent in forecast owner earnings, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Near-term refinancing could change the interest cost embedded in equity owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Computed annual cash interest decreased approximately $1.03 million pre-tax: from $30.40 million on the former debt to $29.375 million on the new notes; fees and bridge-cash effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Equity-level owner earnings retain interest expense, while refinancing fees or cash used at closing affect the cash bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: On November 6, 2020, Academy, Ltd. issued $ 400.0 million of 6.00 % senior secured notes which are due November 15, 2027 (the “Notes”), pursuant to an indenture, dated as of November 6, 2020 (the “Indenture”), with Academy, Ltd. the Guarantors (as defined below) and The Bank of New York Mellon Trust Company, N.A., as trustee and collateral agent (in such capacity, the “Notes Collateral Agent”).
audit_findings.explanation: This is no longer merely prospective: the May 14, 2026 refinancing replaced $485 million of debt with $500 million of 5.875% notes. The recurring interest change is small—about 0.9% of the anchor and approximately $0.17 per share of base value after applying the first-quarter 23.5% tax rate and the model's base cash-flow multiple. The direction is mixed because lower recurring interest raises value while closing fees or reduced cash lower it.
audit_findings.action: Update future interest to the 5.875% notes, obtain the refinancing closing statement and post-closing cash balance, purge nonrecurring fees from owner earnings, and ensure any cash effect is reflected once in the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Some cash added to equity value may be required insurance liquidity
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash legally or operationally required to secure captive-insurance claims is not distributable and should not receive a dollar-for-dollar equity bridge addition unless matching obligations are otherwise reflected.
audit_findings.evidence: The Captive must maintain a sufficient level of liquidity to fund future reserve payments and secure the insurer's obligations for workers compensation, Texas non-subscriber, general liability, directors and officers liability, employment practices liability, and medical stop-loss programs.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates a captive-liquidity requirement but does not disclose the captive's cash or minimum required capital at May 2. The possible amount is bounded by the $337.81 million total cash bridge, equal to $5.08 per share or 17.8% of base equity value, so materiality cannot be dismissed; however, the record does not show that anything close to that amount is unavailable. The filed January 31 self-insurance reserve of $29.225 million is not itself proof of captive cash restrictions.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the captive's May 2 statutory balance sheet, regulatory capital requirement, collateral or letter-of-credit schedule, claims reserves, and intercompany balances; exclude only demonstrably unavailable cash and rerun the bridge.
